summary: VPN split-tunnel rewrites DNS to internal IPs; OCSP/CRL blocked -> mtls token-refresh loop and intermittent 5xx on private deployment
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 5xx errors from Redwood control plane and repeated model pull auth failures after enabling a remote-office VPN split-tunnel. The customer's network team has confirmed DNS responses for Redwood endpoints are rewritten to internal addresses by the VPN appliance. Simultaneously OCSP and CRL endpoints are not reachable (blocked by egress policy), causing mTLS client cert validation and token refresh to fail intermittently, leading to a control-plane token-refresh loop and downstream 5xxs on serving nodes.

Impact: Model pulls failing, streaming sessions reset, and increased control-plane auth retries for both control-plane RPCs and artifact downloads. Customer reports production traffic degraded for 25% of requests originating from the impacted office during their business hours.

Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed VPC peering to Redwood control plane), production, us-east-1. Customer uses branch-office VPN (split-tunnel) that rewrites corporate DNS to internal forwarder when connecting.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Establish VPN connection to branch office with split-tunnel enabled. 2) From a node inside the customer's private deployment that uses branch-office DNS, resolve control-plane hostname (control.redwood-inference.internal). 3) Observe DNS answer rewritten to an internal IP (10.50.200.x) that routes to a local proxy. 4) Attempt model pull or control-plane auth handshake. 5) Observe mTLS validation falling back to OCSP/CRL; remote OCSP endpoints are unreachable due to egress ACLs. 6) Reproduce partial 5xx or token-refresh loop.

Notes: Reproduction is intermittent — high likelihood when branch-office DNS forwards to a transparent HTTP-proxy that returns cached CNAMEs and blocks outbound TCP/443 to OCSP responder hosts.
observed_behavior:
- DNS responses for Redwood hostnames are resolved to internal IPs (split-horizon).
- HTTP/gRPC connections to control plane successfully connect to the internal proxy but fail mTLS validation because OCSP stapling/validation cannot complete (OCSP endpoints blocked).
- Control-plane returns repeated auth transient errors; clients enter token-refresh loops.
- Serving nodes intermittently return 502/504 during artifact fetch and streaming sessions drop with grpc status 14.
- Logs show repeated TLS handshake timeouts to ocsp.example-ca.com and 'certificate verification failed: unable to get local issuer certificate' in auth layer.
expected_behavior:
- Customers on VPN split-tunnels should resolve control-plane endpoints to RFC-compliant IPs or have DNS split-horizon that preserves correct external resolution for Redwood hostnames.
- OCSP/CRL endpoints must be reachable from serving nodes; mTLS validation should succeed and not cause token refresh loops.
- No application-layer 5xxs from control-plane due to downstream DNS/OCSP blocking.
logs_and_evidence:
- tcpdump from serving node: repeated SYN->SYN-ACK->RST to ocsp.example-ca.com on 443, no application-layer response.
- agent logs: 'ocsp fetch failed: timeout' and 'auth: client cert revocation check failed'.
- control-plane trace id: cp-trace-20260310-58a7 (customer-provided).
- Customer provided VPN appliance config screenshot showing DNS rewrite rule and internal forwarder IP 10.50.200.5.
- Packet capture shows DNS A response contains internal IP for control.redwood.example.com and an immediate HTTP CONNECT to a transparent proxy.
investigation_notes:
- Confirmed split-horizon DNS rewrite on customer's VPN appliance returns internal IPs for Redwood hosts.
- Confirmed OCSP endpoints (e.g., ocsp.example-ca.com) are blocked by branch egress ACL; traceroute from branch edge drops at customer edge.
- Hypothesis: internal proxy returns altered SNI or terminates TLS for client requests, returning cached content/redirects that break control-plane mTLS expectations.
- Related to SUP-421420 (token-refresh loops caused by stale DNS) — customer-specific variant due to split-tunnel + OCSP block.
- Reached out to SRE to validate whether Redwood control-plane has fallback behaviour for missing OCSP responses (we currently treat OCSP fetch failures as transient and retry; in this case retries exacerbate token churn).
mitigation:
Short-term recommendations provided to customer: 
- Disable DNS rewrite rule for Redwood hostnames in VPN appliance (allow external resolution).
- Allow outbound access to OCSP and CRL endpoints (tcp/443 to ocsp.* and tcp/80/tcp/443 to CRL hosts) from branch office egress.
- As a stopgap, route control-plane hostnames via the company's DNS resolver to ensure external resolution (split-horizon bypass).

Redwood actions in progress: 
- SRE to add a temporary control-plane tolerance change to reduce token-refresh retry storm for customers that report OCSP timeouts.
- Product to add doc guidance for Private deployments behind split-tunnel VPNs explaining required egress allowlist (OCSP, CRL, control-plane IPs, SNI-preserving proxies).
resolution:
Workaround accepted by customer on 2026-03-12: customer disabled DNS rewrite for control-plane hostnames and opened egress to OCSP endpoints. After change, auth failures dropped to baseline and serving-node 5xxs ceased.
Follow-up: Redwood to publish a short runbook for Private/VPN network teams and update onboarding checklist. Issue will be Closed after runbook published and customer verifies stability for 72h.
